newsitem.title: CHINA: China customs seizes 370 kg of drugs in 1996.
newsitem.headline: China customs seizes 370 kg of drugs in 1996.

text.p: Chinese customs authorities solved 134 drug-trafficking cases and seized 370.2 kg (816 lb) of narcotics in 1996, the Xinhua news agency said on Thursday.
The amount of drugs confiscated last year was nearly six times that seized in 1995, Xinhua said.
Customs officials also confiscated 6.24 kg (13.7 lb) of hallucinogens and 12 tonnes of chemicals used for processing drugs, the agency said. It gave no details.

In southwestern Yunnan province, which borders the Golden Triangle drug production area where Thailand, Burma and Laos converge, customs officials had confiscated 23 kg (51 lb) of drugs in border checks, it said.
Officials in Yunnan's capital Kunming had seized a total of 20 kg (44.1 lb) of drugs sent through the post, it said.
Last week, officials told a national conference on banned drugs that Chinese police had arrested more than 110,000 people for drug-related crimes and solved more than 87,000 narcotics cases in 1996.
Police seized more than four tonnes of heroin, more than 1.7 tonnes of opium and more than one tonne of amphetamines, or "ice" last year, Xinhua quoted the officials as saying.
Drug abuse, nearly wiped out under the puritan rule of Mao Zedong, has returned in China since market-oriented economic reforms loosened the central government's control over society.
Drug cartels operating out of the Golden Triangle have increasingly used China as a transit route for drug shipments to Hong Kong and then on to North America and Europe.
